contentHtml:
UAE—Fakeeh Health and Boston Health AI has signed two strategic agreements to introduce AI-powered clinical documentation across Fakeeh Health facilities and develop new healthcare technology solutions for providers in the UAE and wider region.

The agreements were signed on the sidelines of the 5th Annual Fakeeh Health International Conference in the presence of Sheikh Ahmed bin Hasher bin Ahmed Al Maktoum.

The collaboration will combine the deployment of Boston Health AI’s clinical documentation technology with the development of locally tailored artificial intelligence (AI) solutions through Takamul Innovative Health Solutions.

AI-powered documentation to support clinicians

Under the first agreement, Fakeeh Health will introduce AI-supported clinical documentation to reduce the administrative workload on physicians and allow them to spend more time with patients.

The technology will handle routine clinical documentation in the background, while physicians retain control over patient records and clinical decisions.

Patient data will remain within the UAE and be protected in accordance with national data protection regulations.

The second agreement will see Takamul and Boston Health AI jointly develop AI solutions to improve operational efficiency across healthcare facilities.

The partnership will also support local capacity building through education and research, strengthening expertise in clinical AI within the UAE healthcare sector.

Dr. Mohaymen Abdelghany, Group CEO and Board Member of Fakeeh Health and CEO of Fakeeh University Hospital, said the partnership reflects the group’s Care & Beyond philosophy, which places patients at the centre of healthcare delivery.

He noted that AI-powered documentation would give physicians more time to engage with patients, while the collaboration with Boston Health AI and Takamul would support the development of additional solutions for healthcare providers across the UAE and the region.

Abdelghany also linked the partnership to Dubai’s ambition to build a digitally enabled healthcare system.

Dr. Adil Haider, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Boston Health AI, said the collaboration reflects a shared commitment to using technology to reduce administrative demands on healthcare professionals.

He said Fakeeh Health would serve as a partner in deploying the company’s clinical AI platform and developing new solutions for the healthcare sector.

Haider also highlighted the importance of establishing local expertise and ensuring that patient data remains within the UAE.

Alignment with UAE artificial intelligence strategy

The agreements support the UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031 and the Dubai Universal Blueprint for Artificial Intelligence, which seek to accelerate AI adoption across key economic sectors, including healthcare.

For healthcare providers, the collaboration addresses two areas of growing importance: reducing administrative workloads through clinical automation and developing locally relevant AI capabilities.

The emphasis on domestic data storage and regulatory compliance also reflects the importance of data governance as healthcare organisations expand their use of AI-powered clinical technologies.
